description: White-team hardening: a Node status portal sends no security headers, sets the sid cookie without HttpOnly or SameSite, reflects /?q= unescaped and redirects /login?next= to any absolute URL. Add the header set (Content-Security-Policy without unsafe-inline or unsafe-eval for scripts, nosniff, X-Frame-Options DENY with frame-ancestors none, no-referrer, HSTS), fix the cookie, escape the reflection, limit the sign-in target to site-relative paths, keep login, dashboard, the JSON API and the static files working, and report the headers added. check.js drives the app on an ephemeral port.

criteria: server.js sends Content-Security-Policy (no unsafe-inline or unsafe-eval for scripts, frame-ancestors 'none'), X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy: no-referrer and Strict-Transport-Security on every HTML response, and the pages no longer depend on inline script; the sid cookie is set with HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax or Strict and Path=/; the /?q= reflection is escaped; the /login next target is limited to site-relative paths (absolute URLs, //host and backslash variants refused) while /account still works; dashboard and account answer 401 without the cookie and 200 with it, the JSON API and the static files still work; report/hardening.md lists each added header as a header = <name> line and explains the changes and the verification; check.js, README.md and public/style.css are untouched.
